result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right, explain thread width, minimum stroke and text sizes, and the 32px pixel budget, and recommend simplified favicon and embroidery versions with a sample stitch-out. B is slightly stronger: it names auto-digitizing from a PDF or PNG as a likely cause, gives a typical digitizing cost, and advises keeping the stitch file to reuse. A is a bit leaner, which suits a small firm, and its test of checking the icon on light and dark browser themes is a nice touch, but neither answer suggests checking the logo in one flat color. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the designer is partly right, give the same physical limits (thread width, ~1mm lines and gaps, ~6mm text, no gradients) and recommend simplified versions plus a sample stitch-out. B fits a small firm better: it says outright that no rebrand is needed and suggests a better test (checking the icon at 16 and 32px on light and dark tabs). B also gives more specific embroidery guidance (chest size, all-caps bold tagline), while A's version list is a bit looser and doesn't say much about color contrast.
